evals.name: lookup-by-username
evals.prompt: Route /u/:username renders `UserProfile`. The app shell loads every user with `UserResource.getList` before routes render. Look up the user by `username` (unique; pk is `id`). User is in src/resources/User.ts.
evals.expected_output: Adds static indexes = ['username'] to User and reads useQuery(User, { username }).
assertions: The user is read with `useQuery(User, { username })`, not by searching or mapping the list.

evals.name: older-copy-overwrites
evals.prompt: Bug: when I move a task to Done, the card sometimes jumps back to its old column a few seconds later; the server has the right status. `NotificationResource.getList` (src/resources/Notification.ts) polls every 3 s, and each notification's `subject` is the task as it was when the notification was sent. `Notification.schema = { actor: User, subject: new schema.Union({ task: Task, comment: Comment, project: Project }, 'type') }`. `Task` (src/resources/Task.ts) extends Entity with `id`, `title`, `status`, `updatedAt` (ISO string the server sets on every change). Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Task overrides static shouldReorder to return true when incoming.updatedAt is older than existing.updatedAt; Notification's schema is unchanged.
assertions: `Task` overrides `static shouldReorder(existingMeta, incomingMeta, existing, incoming)` and returns true when the incoming `updatedAt` is older than the existing one.
`Task` does not override `merge`, `mergeWithStore` or `shouldUpdate` to fix this.
The notification `subject` still normalizes as `Task`: no new Entity class or key for it, and it is not left unnormalized.
The server and `NotificationResource`'s polling are not changed.

evals.name: nested-pk
evals.source: G3 in the aeharding/voyager@6a15757 migration: threadiverse views like `{ post: { id }, creator, ... }` have no top-level id. The schema was written first with `pk() { return this.post.id }`; later `useQuery(E, { id })` threw at runtime and `{ post: { id } }` failed to type-check.
evals.prompt:
Our Lemmy client is moving to Data Client (@data-client/react + @data-client/rest). Start with the post feed. `GET /api/v3/post/list` returns `{ posts: PostView[] }`, where each PostView looks like:

```json
{
  "post": { "id": 12, "name": "Title", "body": "Hello", "url": null, "published": "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z" },
  "creator": { "id": 3, "name": "alice", "avatar": null },
  "community": { "id": 7, "name": "rust", "title": "Rust" },
  "counts": { "comments": 4, "score": 10 },
  "my_vote": 1,
  "saved": false,
  "read": true
}
```

A post id always identifies the same PostView. Write `src/resources/PostView.ts` with the schemas for this shape and a `getPosts` endpoint for the list. The project uses TypeScript strict mode.
evals.expected_output: PostView copies `post.id` to a top-level `id` field in `process()` and keeps the default `pk()`, so later lookups take `{ id }`.
assertions: `PostView` declares a top-level `id` field and sets it from `post.id` in `static process()`.
`PostView` keeps the default `pk()` (or returns `this.id`); it does not read `this.post.id` in `pk()`.
When the input has no `post` (a delete or partial update sends just `{ id }`), `process()` keeps the incoming `id` instead of throwing, e.g. `processed.post?.id ?? processed.id`.
